A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gRNAde research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original gRNAde evaluations on single-state and multi-state RNA design, ablations, and retrospective simulations of ribozyme mutant selection.

after.justification: V5 retains these original results and adds structural evaluations, expanded ablations, and retrospective fitness ranking for the t1 ribozyme subunit.

M1.justification: The proposed backbone featurization, multi-state GVP-GNN encoder, conformer pooling, autoregressive decoder, loss, and sampling procedure remain unchanged in Section 2 and Listing 1. The added invariant-GNN configurations are evaluated as ablations.

E1.justification: V5 extends fitness-ranking evaluation from catalytic subunit 5TU to scaffolding subunit t1, covering 47,504 mutants in Figure 12. RNASolo coverage and the 14-RNA benchmark remain unchanged; the three structural case studies use RNAs already represented in v4.

E2.justification: V5 adds ViennaRNA to the 14-RNA comparison and both aggregate test splits, plus ground-truth-sequence and random-sequence controls in Table 1. These substantially broaden comparison beyond the retained Rosetta/FARNA results and model variants.

E3.justification: V5 adds RhoFold-based C4' RMSD, TM-score, GDT_TS, and designability-threshold percentages. Appendix A introduces evaluations using 100 designs per RNA at temperature 0.5, alongside the retained standard 16-design, temperature-0.1 protocol. Figure 7 revises screening budgets and extends them from 2,000 to 10,493. The stated 'All data' evaluation changes from the multi-state to single-state test set, and one training-length ablation changes from 2,000 to 2,500 nucleotides; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V5 adds invariant-versus-equivariant GNN ablations, extends autoregressive/non-autoregressive comparisons to the single-state split, and evaluates existing ablations using 3D metrics. Figures 8–11 add structural case studies and perplexity-versus-structural-consistency analysis. Conversely, v4's three-state and five-state non-autoregressive ablation rows are absent from v5 Table 1.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across three consistent random seeds and summarize stochastic fitness-ranking strategies using medians and interquartile ranges from 10,000 simulations. Added results retain these practices; changed numerical uncertainties do not establish a change in statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V5 adds extensive 3D scores, baseline results, structural examples, and t1 fitness-ranking outcomes. Some retained aggregate values change beyond rounding: single-state, one-state AR recovery changes from 0.5271 to 0.530, and secondary-structure MCC from 0.5706 to 0.585 (v4 Table 2; v5 Table 1). The original 14-RNA gRNAde, Rosetta, and FARNA entries remain unchanged, with ViennaRNA added at 0.27 overall recovery. 'All data' results accompany a changed stated test split and cannot establish same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, symmetry statements, and Equations 1–3 are retained. The illustrative argument against averaging single-state predictions moves into the FAQ. New empirical metrics and interpretive discussion introduce no formal derivations, proofs, or revised mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and central design, speed, and multi-state claims remain stable. V5's conclusion adds the claim that perplexity correlates with structural recovery. The introduction stops foregrounding partial design as a contribution, although that capability remains described in Section 2.3.

C2.justification: V5 adds substantive interpretations of 3D designability, native-sequence predictions as a reference ceiling, transfer from ribosomal training data, and autoregressive modeling of paired nucleotide constraints. It expands guidance on predictor-dependent sequence selection. It also removes explicit statements about inability to modulate conformational propensities and random selection outperforming gRNAde at larger screening budgets; the latter behavior remains visible in revised Figure 7.

D1.justification: V5 specifies a 3,000-node minibatch limit for the reported GPU-memory figures and eight encoder layers for non-autoregressive models. It also supplies designed sequences with structural examples. These improve implementation and reproduction detail without establishing changes to the underlying retained experiments; code access remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds Shen et al. (2022) for its structure-prediction evaluation and Vicens and Kieft (2022) for RNA structural interactions, while removing Maron et al. (2020). The related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. V5 makes local language corrections, adds an author and affiliation, expands metric and FAQ explanations, and organizes appendix material into dedicated visualization, ablation, results, and figure sections.

P2.justification: V5 adds structural overlays, structural-score plots, and the t1 ranking figure; expands the aggregate table substantially; and adds ViennaRNA to Figure 4. It redraws and promotes the evaluation schematic, relocates the architecture diagram to the appendix, and merges existing multi-state recovery plots while dropping the separate secondary-consistency panel. These materially revise visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V4 evaluates a 3D design method mainly through sequence recovery and secondary structure. V5 addresses this important evidential gap with systematic 3D self-consistency measurements, native/random controls, and structural examples, while expanded ablations and a second fitness landscape strengthen assessment of applicability. Predictor limitations and selected examples constrain biological conclusions, and removing the explicit high-budget caveat weakens balance somewhat. Nevertheless, the added evidence substantially improves the paper's ability to demonstrate and expose limits of design fidelity.
